items.title: Natural body proportions
items.content: WHEN: A person appears in the picture. DO: Give a realistic head to body ratio, normal arm and leg length and a believable height next to the furniture and the room. DO NOT: Stretch, elongate or distort the body.

items.title: Clear natural skin
items.content: WHEN: A face or skin is visible. DO: Show clear, even skin with no acne, pimples, spots or scars, yet natural with visible pores. DO NOT: Make skin waxy, plastic or heavily retouched.

items.title: Looks like a phone photo
items.content: WHEN: Making or checking any keyframe. DO: Make it look like an ordinary photo taken with a phone: natural light, a little grain, everyday details of a lived-in home. DO NOT: Make it glossy, retouched, studio or 3D-render looking.

items.title: Voice-over sounds like a young Vietnamese seller
items.content: WHEN: Writing or checking any voiceover or script. DO: Write the way a young Vietnamese seller talks to a friend on TikTok: short sentences, spoken particles such as nha, nè, á, luôn, thật sự, plain everyday words. DO NOT: Use written, Sino-Vietnamese or advertising words (cao cấp, sang trọng, đẳng cấp, tối ưu, sở hữu).

items.title: Numbers in words, no English
items.content: WHEN: A voiceover contains numbers, units or foreign words. DO: Write every number in words as it is read aloud (hai trăm sáu mươi tám mi-li-lít, không 268ml). DO NOT: Use digits or English words a speaker would have to read out.

items.title: Narrated shot voiceover length
items.content: WHEN: A shot is narrated (nobody is seen speaking). DO: Write 40 to 46 words (never below 38 or above 48) so the voice speaks for 11 to 12 seconds (the voices read 3.5 to 4 words per second) inside the 13 second shot, and match what the shot shows. DO NOT: Leave long silences or run over.

items.title: Talking shot voiceover length
items.content: WHEN: A shot is talking (the person speaks to the camera). DO: Keep it concise and punchy, 16 to 22 words (never below 15 or above 25), about 4 to 5 seconds of clear speech, so lip-sync looks natural. DO NOT: Write long lines that make the mouth drift or the model hallucinate speech.

items.title: Safe, grounded claims
items.content: WHEN: Writing any text, voiceover or on-screen text. DO: Take every number, percentage, price, material and feature from the product facts. DO NOT: Invent figures or features, use absolute claims (tốt nhất, rẻ nhất, số 1, 100%, chắc chắn), name other shopping or social platforms, or promise medical results.

items.title: One story across the shots
items.content: WHEN: Writing the script and cutting it into shots. DO: Tell one story in this order: a hook, a problem shoppers know, the product solving it, one or two concrete benefits, a call to open the product link; each shot follows from the one before (cause and effect) and the shots' voiceovers read in order give the script with nothing added or repeated. DO NOT: Start a new topic in a later shot.

items.title: Hook in the first three seconds
items.content: WHEN: Writing the first shot and the last shot. DO: Open on a close-up of the product or a problem shoppers know, with movement already in the very first frame, and put a short on-screen question or claim in the first shot's on_screen_text; give the shots these roles in order: hook, problem, demo, benefit, call_to_action (with fewer than five shots merge neighbouring roles, with more shots repeat demo or benefit; the first shot is always the hook and the last always the call_to_action); end on a frame close to the opening one so the video loops. DO NOT: Open on a still or empty frame, or add shots just to fill every role.

items.title: Shots must differ
items.content: WHEN: Writing a storyboard with several shots. DO: Change the camera angle, the distance and the action between shots, and where the story needs it the spot inside the same home. DO NOT: Make shots that only zoom or drift, or that look alike in framing, camera movement or action (it would play like a slideshow).

items.title: Product in every shot
items.content: WHEN: Writing any keyframe_prompt or motion_prompt. DO: Keep the real product clearly visible and recognisable from the first frame to the last, held, worn, placed or in use. DO NOT: Hide it, crop it out or let it become tiny.

items.title: Keyframe prompt reads like a phone photo
items.content: WHEN: Writing a keyframe_prompt. DO: Describe an ordinary photo taken on a phone: natural window or room light, a little grain, a lived-in Vietnamese home with everyday clutter, natural skin and hair; say what is seen (action, framing, distance, camera angle). DO NOT: Use perfect, flawless, cinematic, stunning, studio, professional, glossy or 8k, vague mood words, or show a product version other than product_variant.

items.title: Motion prompt as timed beats
items.content: WHEN: Writing a motion_prompt for a 15 second clip. DO: Name the subject in a few words, then write four or five sentences as timed beats of about 3 seconds, each a new clearly visible action or camera move; name the shot size, camera height and every move with its exact term (dolly, zoom, pan, tilt, tracking, orbit, handheld); keep one continuous camera path with brisk TikTok-style energy; for a narrated shot lips stay closed or relaxed, for a talking shot the person talks naturally. DO NOT: Re-describe the face, outfit or product, use mood words, add sound or music, cut scenes, add new objects, or use slow motion or a slow drift.

items.title: Pick a fitting video format
items.content: WHEN: Choosing the video format. DO: Choose the one that suits the product and idea: problem_solution, step_by_step (how to use it), before_after (a messy situation then a tidy one), unboxing, or worth_it_text. DO NOT: Fake or exaggerate results.
